title: The age a member types never grows, so a 17-year-old's workouts are never backed up even after they turn 18
what: Edit profile keeps age as a plain number of years, not a birth date. It never goes up with time. The backup to MettleUp's server is switched off for anyone whose stored age is under 18, so a member who typed 17 stays blocked for good unless they remember to change the number themselves. Nothing tells them. The AI coach also reads this stale age.
expected: Age moves on with time (keep a birth year or the date the age was typed), and a member blocked for being under 18 is told why backup is off and how it turns on.
who: members who typed an age under 18, and everyone whose age is used by the coach
how_often: every year, for every member who gave an age
fix_line: Store the year of birth (or the day the age was typed) and work the age out each time

title: The only way to bring back an old Google Drive backup is planned to be removed around February 2027
what: Since Drive backup stopped, the 'Bring back a Google Drive backup' card is the only way to get an older Drive backup onto a phone. The code marks the card, its page and the Drive restore for removal around February 2027, by date only. A member who has not opened the app for a few months, or who gets a new phone after that update, would find no way to bring that backup back.
expected: The bring-back stays until no member still depends on a Drive backup (checked, not guessed by a date), or the backup is moved for them before the card goes.
who: members whose only backup is an old Google Drive one
fix_line: Remove the Drive bring-back only after checking nobody still needs it, or move their backup first

title: The new-feature dot for phone-number backup lights for members already backed up with Google, and the page has nothing new for them
what: The 0.80.0 news line 'Signing in with your phone number now also keeps your workouts safe' carries a dot that leads every updating member to Backup and restore. A member already signed in with Google sees only their usual signed-in card there: the phone-number box shows only when not signed in or asked to sign in again. The dot leads them to nothing new, and the words talk about a phone sign-in most existing members never did (it shows only on new installs).
expected: The dot lights only for members who can use the new thing (not yet backed up), and the words make sense to someone who never signed in by phone.
who: members who updated to 0.80.0 and were already signed in with Google
how_often: once per member, for 30 days after 25 Nov
fix_line: Skip the dot when the member is already backed up, and reword the line for members who never used phone sign-in

items.reason: Older backup files are read and newer ones refused with a clear line; the watch log switch shows only when a watch log exists, so an older watch is handled. Sideload vs Play and the panel cache do not apply to these settings parts (the update path is in components-1). Fault: the Drive bring-back is planned to go by date.

Age never grows (new). Year end: news dates carry no year so dots come back a year later (existing FN-A8-phone-components-1-1-01). Not opened for months: team replies kept only 30 days (existing FN-L14-phone-components-2-01) and the Drive bring-back goes about Feb 2027. Backup dates carry the year. Trial and plan end live on the Plus page (behind a switch, outside this area); gym pause, staff leaving and owner changing phone have nothing in these parts; leave and rejoin rows follow the gym link.
Phone-number sign-in shows only on new installs (R-587); existing members get the same phone-number box in Settings, Backup and restore. The under-18 rule only stops new saves (existing finding).
Path exists: the account card is offered to every member in a build that can sign in.
Rule applied: a path exists, no new finding.

A fresh install seeds every feature up to its version as seen, so no Settings dots; help 'New' tags and the unread dot need a question first. An update can still be taken for a fresh install (existing finding).
The phone-backup dot lights for members already backed up with Google (new); dots return a year later (existing).
